To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LIS and the enantiomeresplitting were observed for all the studied acyclic terpenoid compounds.
the 13C N M R spectroscopy of ten acyclic monoterpene alcohols in the presence of the chiral lanthanum shift reagent (LAPS) allows the enantiomeration of each compound.
the 13C N M R spectra of ten acyclic alcohols were recorded in the presence of the chiral shift reagent Eu(hfbc)3 and the lanthanide-induced shifts were measured on the carbon signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of novel 2-aryl-3-(2,6-dimethoxyphenyl)-2,3-dihydro-1,4-benzothiazine 1,1-dioxide derivatives (2a-2j).
the development of a new method for the determination of the enantiomeres of acyclic terpens using 13C N.M.R. spectroscopy.
the synthesis and characterization of new lanthanide shift agents (LSAs) for NMR spectroscopy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enantiomorphs of a given compound are not necessarily distinguished by their NMR spectra, and this is true even for the most powerful of the NMR methods, the LIS method, which is used in this work.
a combination of 1H and 13C N‐MR spectroscopies is a very powerful tool for the determination of the stereochemistry at the chiral carbon of acyclic terpens.
the LIS and the splitting are both dependent on the distance between the binding function, the double bonds and the considered carbon, but the LIS is also affected by the number of bonds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LIS is an efficient tool for enantiomeric discrimination, which is complementary to the use of chiral derivatizing agents.
the 13C N‐MR spectroscopy is a powerful tool in enantiomeric determination and differentiation.
the LIS of the carbons is a good parameter for the differentiation of the two enantiomers, whereas the enantioméric splitting is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LIS of carbons decreases with the number of carbon atoms between the binding function (alcohol or carboxylic acid) and the considered carbon.
the lanthanide-induced shift (LIS), which is the chemical shift of a nucleus in the presence of the lanthanide, is a very useful parameter in the enantiomorph differentiation of acyclic molecules.
the enantiodiscrimination of a wide variety of acyclic terpens by NMR spectroscopy is possible.
